Question: When iaso asks a question during a benchmark run and no owner is there, who should answer it, and should there be a cap on how many questions or turns a run gets?

You said on 2026-10-21: "The idea is to be able from one iaso dev command like iaso evaluate simple or iaso evaluate complex to be able to run this benchmark test and see how much haiku or Sonnet is able to implement autonomously using iaso tools."
Options: No answer, the question is logged as unanswered (Recommended) (The run continues with the next scripted request and the unanswered question is counted in the score. No model plays the owner. Recommended: You asked to see how much Haiku or Sonnet can do on its own, so an unanswered question scored as a gap is closest to that.); A cheap model plays the owner from a hidden brief (A second model answers from a brief you write. Its answers can steer the run, and it may need a cap on exchanges.)
Answer: How can no owner be there exactly? There should always be a question owner in my opinion. A model answers the questions of the other one.

Question: Should a benchmark run have a limit on how many questions the model playing the owner answers, or on how many turns or minutes a run may take? If yes, what limit do you want?

You said on 21 Oct: "There should always be a question owner in my opinion. A model answers the questions of the other one."
Options: Set a limit you name (Recommended) (A run stops answering after the number of questions or turns you give, and the questions beyond it are counted as unanswered. Recommended: You asked for one command to measure how much the model can do on its own, and a run with no limit could run indefinitely. A limit you name keeps the cost bounded without guessing a number for you.); No limit (The model playing the owner answers every question the agent asks, and a run is not cut short by a cap.)
Answer: Both should be possible. If unspecified, questiontool needs to ask the question.
